Use case: style-transfer. Asset type: a single fine-line architectural illustration for the Chinese heritage collection 访古.
Image 1 is the STYLE MASTER, an existing Vairocana Buddha contour drawing. Match its elegant, delicate, slightly organic thin lines, restrained detail, generous blank areas, and consistent visual density. Image 2 (and subsequent photos if applicable) is SUBJECT GEOMETRY ONLY: draw the actual named monument in that reference, preserving its identifying silhouette, roof type, visible storey count, bay count, openings, and proportions.
Create a refined, sparse BLACK INK ON PURE WHITE line drawing. Use confident fine contours with a few finer internal structural lines. All surfaces remain WHITE; use outlines for doors and windows rather than dark fills. No solid shadows, no broad grey shading, no crosshatching, no pencil grain, no texture, no gradient. No color, no gold, no black background. The white will become transparent and the ink the relevant dynasty color in the website.
Show the complete monument, centered, approximately straight-on at facade level, with verticals vertical and minimal perspective. Use only a few short ground lines. Remove tourists, foliage, vehicles, wires, modern signage, fences obstructing the structure, neighboring distractions and sky. Preserve architectural ornament selectively, without filling every roof tile or brick. No invented features. No labels, letters, calligraphy, dimension lines, captions, watermark, frame or border.
Wide compositions: landscape 1536×1024, entire building occupies about 82% of canvas width, roof/apex and base uncut, balanced breathing room. Tall pagodas: portrait 1024×1536, entire pagoda occupies about 82% of height, centred with equal side margins, apex and base uncut.


SUBJECT: ONLY Xitiansi Stone Hall of Jijian Temple on Tianchi Mountain, Suzhou (天池山寂鉴寺西天寺石殿), constructed1357. Image2 shows its full silhouette with a tree obstruction; Image3 is a clear frontal close-up of the SAME hall. Draw ONLY the low grey STONE hall in the foreground of these photos, NOT the yellow plaster rooms behind it and NOT a separate one-bay stone shrine. The hall is three bays, with exactly FOUR thick squared stone piers across the front creating THREE rectangular door openings, the central opening slightly narrower in current door fittings; plain monolithic stone lintels and slab wall planes. Preserve exactly ONE very low shallow hip-and-gable stone roof, composed of LARGE FLAT STONE SLABS, NO CHINESE CLAY ROOF-TILE PATTERN. The roof has an extremely long straight ridge, two plain weathered upturned ends, and a sweeping slightly upturned continuous eave. Keep the actual squat wide proportions and the heavy slab-thickness at the eave. There are no elaborate timber bracket clusters. Make verticals vertical, near straight-on centered facade, complete the eave tips from the full-view photo. Plain blank plaques and a very few representative door-panel vertical grooves; doors open as white empty openings, no religious figures or shrine clutter. Remove tree trunk, rocks outside the hall, vegetation, yellow rear rooms, fire equipment, metal basins, signs and tourists. Keep only the very low threshold foundation and two short ground lines. Roof and wall planes WHITE, no mottled stone texture, no brick grid, no crosshatching. Delicate contour lines, sparse like mother. Entire low hall must fit within x150 to x1386 of1536x1024canvas with visibly ample blank margins and no cropping.

site_recommendation.name: 寂鉴寺石殿
site_recommendation.sub: 苏州 · 天池山西天寺
site_recommendation.place: 江苏 · 苏州 · 天池山
site_recommendation.lede: 寂鉴寺的西天寺石殿紧挨山岩，以石柱、石枋与大片石板摹写木构殿宇。浅缓的屋面和三间开口使这座元代石殿显得低平而紧凑。
facts: 西天寺石殿建于元至正十七年（1357），与旁侧兜率宫、极乐园小石屋分别成体。
正殿面阔三间约7.64米、进深两间约5.52米，单檐歇山，平面呈凸字形。
除供出入的格扇门外，主要构件以石材仿木雕凿，后部紧靠天然山岩。
